answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake bonds to audit peers across a cluster network. Topological cut verifications isolate suspicious subgraphs, triggering multi-agent consensus audits that slash dishonest stakes. When clusters fragment, a malicious identity cannot hide: audit intensity escalates in a cost spiral where attacker expenditure scales superlinear with fake identities, reducing fraudulent returns to a velvet relic of failed subversion.
